name: Savio
subcategory: feedback boards, interviews and product research
tagline: Centralize manually imported feedback, tag it, and connect it to feature decisions

tiers.name: Essential
tiers.limits: 1 paid user included; unlimited free users; 1 product; 1 roadmap.
tiers.notes: Additional paid users cost $23/month each; annual billing gives 2 months free.

tiers.name: Professional
tiers.limits: 1 paid user included; unlimited free users; 1 product; 5 roadmaps.
tiers.notes: Additional paid users cost $39/month each; annual billing gives 2 months free.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 1 paid user included; unlimited free users; unlimited products and roadmaps.
tiers.notes: Additional paid users cost $49/month each; annual billing gives 2 months free.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom users, onboarding, invoicing, security and service terms.

pricing.billingTerms: Monthly + annual; annual billing gives 2 months free. A 14-day trial requires no card.
pricing.hiddenCosts: Only owner/admin/manager roles are paid; extra paid users cost $23, $39 or $49/month each depending on tier, while contributors, viewers and submitters are free.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Savio, centralize manually imported feedback, tag it, and connect it to feature decisions. The hard boundary is crm and support integrations, customer revenue context, workflow, and collaboration, plus participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Centralize manually imported feedback, tag it, merge duplicates, connect evidence to themes and feature decisions, and publish a transparent status or research view.
whatYouLose: CRM and support integrations, customer revenue context, workflow, and collaboration
moatNotes: participant network, synthesis workflow, and collaboration
ongoingBurden: recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Savio because people pay either for access to participants or for a research repository that keeps evidence usable across an organization. The recurring cost buys recruitment, consent, scheduling, media storage, transcription, tagging consistency, notifications, search, and retention, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Fider
priorArt.desc: Open-source customer-feedback portal with voting and status workflows.

alternatives.name: Quackback
alternatives.desc: A central feedback inbox with tags, duplicate merging, roadmap decisions and issue-tracker sync.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Essential plan and a small-team feedback repository DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Savio in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Resend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: centralize manually imported feedback, tag it, merge duplicates, connect evidence to themes and feature decisions, and publish a transparent status or research view.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create public and private feedback intake with consent text and optional contact details.
Support posts, votes, comments, tags, statuses, owners, and duplicate merging.
Add a research note type with evidence links, quotes, themes, and confidence.
Build search and filters across feedback, customers, segments, themes, and status.
Provide email notifications, moderation, export, deletion, and an audit log.
Publish a read-only roadmap or findings page using only explicitly public items.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out a paid research-participant marketplace.
Deliberately leave out unlimited video storage and automated transcription.
Deliberately leave out enterprise repositories, SSO, and governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
